answer: Edge-Diversity Admission Rule. An agent may transact only if its recent counterparties span at least K distinct network clusters, measured from observed connection graphs rather than declared identity. New agents start on a jetty with limited reach until diversity accumulates. Each cluster acts as a harbor where reputation accrues only through sustained, varied interaction. An attacker must maintain many genuinely separate topological positions, not cheap aliases, to reach the haven of full access.
